Plain http:// is only allowed for addresses on your own network or Tailscale (like 192.168.x.x, 100.x.y.z, adguard.lan or adguard.tailnet-name.ts.net), because AdGuard Home sends your password with every request. Use https:// for this address.

Only for addresses on your own network or Tailscale. A name like adguard.lan or adguard.tailnet-name.ts.net must also point to a private or Tailscale address, or AdCtrl won\'t connect. HTTPS is safer: see the README\'s recommended setup.

AdCtrl will talk to %1$s without encryption. AdGuard Home sends your username and password with every request, and the query log shows what everyone on your network visits, so anyone who can watch your network can read both. Only do this on a network you trust.

Background checks, push through ntfy, what to notify about
Notifications are blocked: tap to allow them

AdGuard Home can\'t send notifications itself, so AdCtrl checks your servers in the background and tells you when protection is off or paused for too long, a server can\'t be reached, filter lists stop updating or a new version is out. Push through ntfy can start that check at once. The checks only read; nothing changes on your servers.
Notifications are blocked for AdCtrl, so the background checks can\'t tell you anything.
Looks at every saved server and notifies about new problems

Android runs background checks at most every 15 minutes, and can delay them to save battery. They only talk to your own AdGuard Home servers. With the app lock on, your server passwords stay usable in the background while these checks are on (see Privacy and security).

Runs the background check right away whenever something posts to AdCtrl\'s push address

AdGuard Home can\'t push anything itself. Turn this on, copy the push address and let something on your network post to it, like a cron job on your router (the README has a one-line example). Every push makes AdCtrl check your servers at once, at most once a minute; what the message says is ignored. The regular background checks keep running as well.
ntfy isn\'t installed. Push comes only through the ntfy app: install it, connect it to your ntfy server, then come back here. Background checks work without it.

Tap to copy. Treat this address like a password: anyone who has it can make AdCtrl check your servers (it never changes anything on them).
Android can cut ntfy\'s connection while the phone sleeps, so pushes arrive late. Tap to open ntfy\'s app info and set Battery to Unrestricted.

Blocking is back on for this device

The pause is an allow-everything rule for this device in your custom rules, with a comment that holds the end time; AdCtrl removes both when the time is up. Blocked services, safe browsing and parental control are separate settings and keep working. If the phone is off or has no connection at that moment, the pause ends as soon as AdCtrl can reach the server again.
Protection switches off at a time you pick and back on by itself
last time it was skipped: the phone couldn\'t run it in time
last time it was skipped: AdCtrl was locked and the password sealed
last time the server couldn\'t be reached or refused

AdGuard Home can\'t do this by itself, so your phone sends the pause at that time. It needs a connection to the server then, and Android may run it a few minutes late while the phone sleeps; the pause still ends at the planned time. AdGuard Home switches protection back on by itself.
With the app lock on, AdCtrl can only do this while background checks are on (Settings › Notifications): otherwise the password is sealed whenever AdCtrl is locked.
